subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Myeloma cytogenetic risk, renal failure induction and IMiD potency with safety

steps.tx: Multiple myeloma (a cancer of plasma cells) splits by chromosomes into two camps. **Standard risk** means hyperdiploidy (extra copies of odd numbered chromosomes, sometimes called triploidy), **t(11;14)** or t(6;14). **High risk** means t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), del(17p) (loss of the short arm of chromosome 17) or gain of 1q21 (an extra piece of chromosome 1). The group decides intensity of therapy and transplant planning.
steps.say: Every new myeloma patient needs a FISH test on the marrow, because the chromosomes found there decide the whole strategy. Extra odd chromosomes or the eleven fourteen swap are grouped in the standard camp with a gentler course. Swaps involving chromosomes four, sixteen or twenty, loss of seventeen p, or extra chromosome one material place the patient in the high risk camp that needs the most aggressive plan available.

steps.tx: The t(11;14) swap overproduces **cyclin D1** (a cell cycle accelerator encoded by CCND1) and makes the cell addicted to **BCL2** (a survival protein), which is why the BCL2 blocker **venetoclax** works strikingly in t(11;14) myeloma after other options fail. High risk swaps instead activate growth drivers such as FGFR3 with MMSET in t(4;14) and MAF in t(14;16), which venetoclax cannot touch.
steps.say: The eleven fourteen swap is the friendly face of myeloma genetics for a second reason beyond good prognosis: it creates a drug target. These cells lean heavily on the survival protein BCL2, so blocking BCL2 with venetoclax kills them even late in the disease. The dangerous swaps work through completely different growth drivers, which is why venetoclax is reserved for the eleven fourteen group.

steps.tx: Myeloma presenting with acute kidney injury (**myeloma kidney** from light chain casts blocking tubules) plus hypercalcaemia (high blood calcium) needs immediate **VCD** (bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone, also called CyBorD), with daratumumab added where available, alongside vigorous saline hydration. Bortezomib and cyclophosphamide clear hepatically (through the liver) so they need no renal dose cut, while full dose **lenalidomide** (renally cleared by the kidneys) would cause crushing marrow suppression and must be avoided.
steps.say: A myeloma patient arriving with failing kidneys and high calcium is an emergency measured in hours, because every day of clogged tubules kills nephrons permanently. The answer is bortezomib based treatment started at once, since both bortezomib and cyclophosphamide bypass the kidneys during clearance. Lenalidomide is the trap here: normal doses in renal failure accumulate and wipe out the blood counts, so it stays out of the regimen.

steps.tx: **IMiDs** (immunomodulatory drugs) grip cereblon (a protein switch) and destroy the transcription factors Ikaros and Aiolos (IKZF1 and IKZF3, controllers of myeloma growth). Potency climbs across generations: thalidomide, then lenalidomide, then **pomalidomide** at roughly 10 times lenalidomide and 100 times thalidomide. Pomalidomide breaks lenalidomide resistance and is processed by liver CYP enzymes (drug metabolising proteins), so it stays safe and full dose in kidney failure.
steps.say: All three sibling drugs share one clever mechanism: they reprogram the cell's own waste disposal to shred two proteins myeloma cannot live without. Each generation grips that machinery tighter, with pomalidomide the strongest by far, rescuing patients whose disease outgrew lenalidomide. Its liver based breakdown is the practical pearl: when kidneys fail, pomalidomide keeps working at full strength while lenalidomide needs cutting.

vis.alt: Illustration of marrow plasmacytosis with CRAB features and IMiD, proteasome and CD38 drug mechanisms.
vis.caption: IMiD action through cereblon among plasma cell drug mechanisms. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Every IMiD prescription needs clot cover, because all three raise venous thrombosis (vein clot) risk and demand **thromboprophylaxis** (aspirin or heparin type blood thinners). Neutropenia (low neutrophils) dominates pomalidomide and lenalidomide, needing count checks and dose holds, while painful neuropathy (nerve damage) belongs chiefly to thalidomide. Pomalidomide runs 4 mg on days 1 to 21 of each 28 day cycle.
steps.say: Prescribing these drugs safely means managing three toxicities by name. Clots threaten with every member of the family, so blood thinners start alongside the myeloma drug. Falling neutrophils plague the two newer siblings, so counts are watched and doses paused on schedule. Nerve pain is mostly the oldest sibling's fault, which is why thalidomide has faded from modern induction while pomalidomide leads at relapse.

rows: Aspirin or anticoagulant with every cycle
Count checks; hold or cut dose
Prefer newer IMiDs; stop if painful
